newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.06 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.06 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.06 percent to close at 1.0206 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency at 1.0205 to 1.0255 per dollar, dealers said.
The Central Bank set the new real-dollar mini-band through a buy/sell auction before the open. The previous trade level was set on Wednesday at between 1.020 and 1.025 reais to the dollar.
Dealers said the market is expecting for Monday another decline in the dollar-real mini-band between 0.05 and 0.1 percent.
A limited strike by bank workers begun on Thursday weakened trade again today, they said.
Although the strike failed to close banks, some of them could not participate in the forex market because their back-offices were not operating, dealers said.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real dropped 0.07 percent to end at 1.0264 real per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed steady at 1.038 real per greenback, traders said.
